newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg has profit amid difficult U.S. cereal market.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg has profit amid difficult U.S. cereal market.

text.p: Kellogg Co. Friday reported a profit for the fourth quarter, reversing a year-ago loss, but cited difficult U.S. and British business environments for its ready-to-eat cereals.
Overall, the nation's No. 1 cereal company said its global volume grew 2 percent in the fourth quarter and by 1 percent for all of 1996.
However, the growth was most noticable outside the United States.

"During the quarter, we achieved excellent growth in our convenience foods business and solid growth in our ready-to-eat cereal business outside the United States and the United Kingdom," Chairman Arnold Langbo said in a statement. "While the U.S. and the U.K. remain challenging, we are encouraged by the contribution of new cereal products in both markets.
He added that the launch of more new cereal products in 1997 should add further strength to Kellogg's U.S. business.

"In 1996, our convenience foods volume grew at a double-digit rate for the second consecutive year," Langbo said. "We look forward to the continued growth of this business, both in the U.S., where we have recently acquired Lender's Bagels, and through expansion to new international markets."

Kellogg reported fourth-quarter earnings of $87.3 million, or 42 cents a share, up from a loss of $71.6 million, or 33 cents a share, a year earlier. Before one-time pre-tax charges in each period for productivity and streamlining initiatives, Kellogg earned 78 cents a share, up from 77 cents a share a year earlier.
Kellogg said initiatives it took in 1995 and 1996 are expected to generate about $160 million in savings in 1997 and future years.
For the year, Kellogg had a profit of $531 million, or $2.50 a share, compared with a profit of $490.3 million, or $2.24 a share, a year earlier.
Revenues for the quarter were $1.56 billion, compared with $1.66 billion a year earlier. For the year, revenues were $6.68 billion, down from $7.00 billion in 1995.
Kellogg's stock gained $1.125 to $69.125 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
